summary: Antje Barth opens by emphasizing AWS's belief that virtually every customer experience will be reinvented with AI agents. She shares that Amazon has over 1,000 generative AI applications built or in development. The most ambitious deployment is Alexa Plus, running hundreds of specialized expert systems across 600 million devices and tens of thousands of partner services. She demonstrates Amazon Q Developer's CLI agent, which integrates with MCP to connect to AWS documentation, revealing it was built and shipped in just 3 weeks. To enable rapid development, AWS adopted a model-driven approach leveraging modern LLMs' reasoning and planning capabilities. AWS released Strands Agents, an open-source Python SDK named by AI itself, integrating with Amazon Bedrock using Claude 3.7 Sonnet but supporting multiple providers including Llama, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, and LiteLLM. It ships with 20+ pre-built tools including memory/RAG, multimodality, deep reasoning, and multi-agent workflows. An internal AWS agent manages over 6,000 tools by storing descriptions in a knowledge base and using semantic retrieval. For scaling MCP from local to cloud, Barth demonstrates deploying a D&D dice-rolling MCP server as a Lambda function using AWS SAM, with DynamoDB for session storage and an API Gateway URL for access. The client side uses Strands Agents with MCP integration, passing a bearer token for authorization. The demo successfully rolls a d20 and returns a seven. She highlights that Lambda deployment grants access to all AWS features. Looking forward, she discusses agent-to-agent communication as the next frontier, notes AWS joined the MCP steering committee and is actively contributing code, and references a colleague's vision that the atomic unit of all digital interactions will be an agent call, imagining personal agents connecting to an agent store to accomplish tasks together.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

AWS joined the MCP steering committee and is actively contributing code to help evolve the protocol
The envisioned future involves personal agents connecting to an agent store to collaboratively accomplish tasks for users

Learn the model-driven approach to agent development that focuses on what agents should do rather than how

sections.title: Introduction and Amazon's AI Scale
sections.summary: Barth introduces the topic of building agents at cloud scale, highlighting Amazon's 1,000+ generative AI applications and the reimagining of Alexa as the largest integration of agentic capabilities, with 600 million devices and hundreds of expert systems.

sections.title: Amazon Q Developer CLI Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates Amazon Q Developer CLI agent integrating with MCP to connect to AWS documentation, revealing the service was built and shipped in 3 weeks, emphasizing execution speed in AI.

sections.title: Strands Agents SDK Introduction
sections.summary: Introduces Strands Agents, an open-source Python SDK with a model-driven approach, 20+ pre-built tools, multi-provider support (Bedrock, Llama, Anthropic, OpenAI, LiteLLM), and native MCP integration. Covers tool retrieval, multimodality, and multi-agent workflows.

sections.title: MCP Scaling: From Local to Cloud
sections.summary: Discusses challenges of scaling MCP from local standard IO to cloud deployment using Lambda functions with streamable HTTP behind an MCP gateway, with authorization. Shows a D&D dice-rolling MCP server code example and mentions the labmc GitHub repo for AWS MCP servers.

sections.title: Cloud MCP Demo and Future Vision
sections.summary: Demonstrates deploying the dice-rolling MCP server as a Lambda function with DynamoDB session storage via AWS SAM, accessed through Strands Agents client with API Gateway URL and bearer token authorization. Highlights AWS's involvement in MCP steering committee, envisions agent-to-agent communication as the next frontier, and closes with a vision of personal agents connecting to an agent store.

demonstrations: Alexa Plus video showing natural language interactions for scheduling, restaurant booking, whale watching, home security camera checks, and Uber integration
Amazon Q Developer CLI demo showing it connecting to an AWS documentation MCP server, requesting permissions, and returning grounded responses about Amazon Bedrock
Strands Agents code walkthrough showing simple install, import, tool addition, and model configuration with Claude 3.7 Sonnet
Standard IO MCP server implementation using Python SDK with FastMCP showing a dice-rolling tool with configurable number of sides

Cloud-scale MCP demo deploying the dice-rolling tool as a Lambda function with DynamoDB session storage via AWS SAM, accessed through Strands Agents client using MCP integration with API Gateway URL and bearer token authorization, successfully rolling a d20 and getting a seven
limitations: 6,000 tools is too many to fit into a single context window for one model to decide among
MCP originally started with standard IO for local connections, creating a scaling challenge for remote/cloud deployment
A2A (agent-to-agent) support for Strands Agents is not yet available but coming soon
The bearer token authorization shown in the demo is a simple concept demo; more robust integrations are needed for production
